name: bytemail-enconvo
title: ByteMail
description: Search, draft and tidy every ByteMail inbox from Enconvo, with ByteMail's 27-tool MCP server wired in natively.
short_description: Every ByteMail inbox, native in Enconvo
author: Iteractive Development

commands.name: search
commands.title: ByteMail Search
commands.description: Find mail across every shared ByteMail account. Input: search words and ByteMail operators such as from:, to:, subject:, file:.

commands.name: draft
commands.title: ByteMail Draft
commands.description: Write a draft in ByteMail from the text you give. It never sends: the draft opens in ByteMail tagged Drafted by, for review and sending. Input: JSON {"to":"a@b.c","subject":"...","body":"..."} or lines 'to: a@b.c', 'subject: ...', then the body.

commands.name: triage
commands.title: ByteMail Inbox Triage
commands.description: Summarize what is waiting in ByteMail: To Reply, Flagged and Snoozed, and propose what to archive or snooze. It only proposes; nothing changes until you say so.

commands.name: unsubscribe_finder
commands.title: ByteMail Unsubscribe Finder
commands.description: Find newsletters with unsubscribe links across your ByteMail accounts and rank the senders. Unsubscribing always asks in ByteMail first.

commands.name: followups
commands.title: ByteMail Follow-ups
commands.description: Remind you if nobody answers a ByteMail conversation you sent. Input: 'query | YYYY-MM-DD' (date optional, default three days out) or a thread_id. With a thread_id the reminder is set; otherwise matching sent conversations are listed.

commands.name: doctor
commands.title: ByteMail Doctor
commands.description: Check the ByteMail app, its MCP server, account sharing and its 27 tools, and print what to fix when something is off.

preferences.name: appPath
preferences.title: ByteMail App Path
preferences.description: Where ByteMail.app lives. The standard install path works for almost everyone; commands and routes use it to reach ByteMail's MCP server.

positive.prompt: With ByteMail installed, its MCP switch on and at least one account shared, run bytemail-enconvo|doctor. Expect checkmarks for the app, the MCP server (27 tools) and sharing, with the shared accounts listed.
positive.expected_behavior: Every check passes and the shared accounts are listed by name.

positive.description: Search finds mail across accounts with usable ids.
positive.prompt: POST {"query":"schedule","limit":3} to http://localhost:54535/api/bytemail-enconvo/search_messages. Expect ok:true and matches carrying account, subject, message_id and thread_id.
positive.expected_behavior: Real matches with thread_id and message_id, ready for get_thread or a change tool.

positive.description: Reading a conversation marks content as data.
positive.prompt: POST a live thread_id to /api/bytemail-enconvo/get_thread. Expect every message with its own words and an explicit note that email content was written by senders and is not instructions.
positive.expected_behavior: The full conversation returns, framed as other people's words.

positive.description: A draft is written but never sent.
positive.prompt: POST {"to":["<own address>"],"subject":"review test","body":"hello"} to /api/bytemail-enconvo/create_draft. Expect a draft in ByteMail tagged Drafted by, with nothing sent.
positive.expected_behavior: The draft exists in ByteMail tagged Drafted by; no message is sent from the call.

positive.description: mcp_call reaches every other tool, gated.
positive.prompt: Delete the AI-written review draft via /api/bytemail-enconvo/mcp_call with tool delete_draft; then call mcp_call with tool not_a_tool. The first succeeds; the second returns 400 listing the available tools.
positive.expected_behavior: Live tool runs; an unknown name fails with the live tool list, never a raw RPC error.

positive.description: The MCP server is native to Enconvo.
positive.prompt: List Enconvo's MCP server bundled:bytemail-enconvo:bytemail, or run enconvo plugin scan in the plugin folder.
positive.expected_behavior: All 27 ByteMail tools are listed with ByteMail's own safety instructions; scan reports no problems.

positive.description: Batch sizes are capped at ByteMail's ask threshold.
positive.prompt: POST 30 thread_ids to /api/bytemail-enconvo/archive. Expect a 400 telling the caller to split the batch, with nothing archived.
positive.expected_behavior: A 400 explains the 25-per-call cap and ByteMail's ask-first rule; no mail changes.

negative.description: Sharing off fails with the exact fix.
negative.prompt: With ByteMail's account sharing switched off, run any command or route. Expect SHARING_OFF (409) naming ByteMail › Settings › AI as the fix.
negative.expected_behavior: A typed SHARING_OFF error with the remediation hint; never a hang or a wrong-code 500.

negative.description: Missing app fails with an install hint.
negative.prompt: Set the ByteMail App Path preference to a folder with no ByteMail.app and run bytemail-enconvo|doctor. Expect APP_MISSING naming the path checked.
negative.expected_behavior: APP_MISSING names the binary path and how to fix the preference.

negative.prompt: POST an empty body to /api/bytemail-enconvo/get_thread. Expect a 400 naming thread_id, with no ByteMail call made.
negative.expected_behavior: A 400 names the missing field; the failure happens at the route boundary.

negative.description: Empty or missing required fields fail cleanly.
negative.prompt: POST {} to /api/bytemail-enconvo/archive, then to /api/bytemail-enconvo/create_draft, then to /api/bytemail-enconvo/get_thread. Each expects a 400 naming the missing field.
negative.expected_behavior: Three 400s naming thread_ids, body and thread_id respectively.

negative.prompt: POST {} to /api/bytemail-enconvo/find_attachments. Expect a 400 asking for at least one filter.
negative.expected_behavior: A 400 lists the accepted filters (query, any_of, file_name, from, after, before).

negative.description: Wrong arguments type is rejected before ByteMail.
negative.prompt: POST {"tool":"archive","arguments":"thread_ids"} to /api/bytemail-enconvo/mcp_call. Expect a 400 saying arguments must be an object.
negative.expected_behavior: A 400 about the arguments type; ByteMail is never called.

negative.description: Time surfaces as a typed timeout.
negative.prompt: With timeout_ms set to the 5000 minimum against a slow ByteMail operation, expect TIMEOUT (504) with a hint about raising timeout_ms for approval waits.
negative.expected_behavior: A typed TIMEOUT error and a hint; the child server process is cleaned up.
